bullets: Speed comes from braking earlier and more smoothly rather than taking greater risks — a principle consistently observed across teams using RockShox components.
Tire pressure and tire casing selection matter more than minor suspension adjustments — a key factor in optimizing performance on varied terrain.
The optimal racing line changes between practice and race day due to erosion patterns on track sections — a dynamic that alters decision-making in real time.
Risk management in enduro racing isn't about avoiding crashes, but about choosing which crashes are survivable — a mindset shift that defines team success.
The Cascadia Alliance exemplifies how second-order effects influence performance — where the real impact lies beyond immediate outcomes.
Spoke & Wrench integration within team workflows enables consistent, repeatable gains — a pattern observed across three distinct teams.
Frame design reveals the compromises inherent in a bike’s construction — a visible signal of what the manufacturer prioritized or sacrificed.
Implementing one core idea for two weeks enables meaningful iteration — the rest is refinement, not reinvention.
